tspan.tspan: Breaking Myths: The Reality of Galaxy's Capabilities and Impact

text.tspan: Gildas Le Corguillé1,2, Anthony Bretaudeau1,3, Björn Grüning4, The Galaxy Community, Wendi Bacon, Bérénice Batut1,5

tspan.tspan: Open science computing is vast and evolving, making workflow managers like
Galaxy essential for reproducible and accessible data analysis.
Established in 2005,
Galaxy
supports diverse scientific domains and is widely
adopted in France, with 10+ servers and UseGalaxy.fr as the national instance.
Despite strong adoption and training resources, misconceptions persist, such as
Galaxy being only for genomics or being difficult to use efficiently for “real”
analysis. To address this, the Galaxy Community works actively on
debunking the

text.tspan: misconceptions.

tspan.tspan: If you have any misconceptions about Galaxy that haven't been addressed yet, or if you'd like to share additional
examples that support its use, please contribute to this discussion. Take a moment to jot down your thoughts on
one of the paper you can find below. Your input is invaluable in helping us debunk misconceptions around Galaxy.
Share Your Insight!

tspan.tspan: Users & PIs

text.tspan: “Galaxy is only useful for teaching, it’s not popular
amongst scientists in academia or industry.””
Galaxy cannot be used on secured data
Galaxy is free to use, so its quality must be poor
because there are no professional staff members.
Galaxy is open-source & open-development, so
there cannot be good documentation or support.
The Galaxy community is full of active and organised professionals, from
software engineers to life scientists.

tspan.tspan: PIs & Core Service Decision-Makers

text.tspan: “Galaxy cannot be sustainable in the long run,
because no commercial organisation is managing it.”
Galaxy tools and supported analyses are out-
dated

tspan.tspan: Combination of automation & testing support, community structure, and user
engagement.
Bring Your Own Compute/Storage/Data (BYOC/S/C), Role-based access
control (RBAC), Single Sign-On (SSO), Identity Federation Protocols, etc.
Online documentation; GitHub issues and PR, Release notes; Galaxy help
forum; Galaxy Training Network with 400+ tutorials, 200+ videos
Project successfully sustained for the last 20 years. Evolving governance and
administrative structures. Sustainability report.
Bioconda and BioContainers, GitHub Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines

text.tspan: Strong governance, diverse funding, user and developer community, and
open-source model make it highly sustainable.
The Galaxy project is extensively documented, with live support and
training.
U
Galaxy’s semi-automatic update infrastructure helps keep tools and
workflows as current as possible while balancing stability and
reproducibility.
Galaxy actually offers numerous benefits and features that can enhance
the productivity and efficiency of technically capable users.
Its user-friendly interface, scalability, and extensive toolset make it ideal
for both education and complex research, as shown by its 500,000+ users,
its use in high-impact studies -cited in 30+ publications every week- and
industry applications.

tspan.tspan: Galaxy is used for sensitive data, both in large scale genomic projects and

text.tspan: in hospitals as it offers a flexible and scalable environment, leveraging
security-enhanced deployment models and access controls.
